questions.question: Which committee is also known as Village and Small Scale Industries Committee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karve Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Karve Committee was established in **1955** to examine and promote the development of village and small-scale industries in India.
 
• It focused on the importance of small-scale industries in generating employment and fostering rural development.
 
• The committee emphasized the need for decentralized production systems to improve rural economies.
 
• Recommendations from the Karve Committee laid the groundwork for various government policies supporting small-scale industries.
 
• The committee highlighted the role of self-employment and traditional skills in strengthening the rural economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Village and Small-Scale Industries:** These industries are integral to the rural economy, providing employment opportunities and reducing urban migration.
 
• **Decentralized Production:** The concept advocated by the Karve Committee aimed to involve rural communities in economic development through localized manufacturing.
 
• **Small-Scale Industries Policy:** Following the Karve Committee's recommendations, the government implemented measures to support small-scale industries, including subsidies and training programs.
 
• **Employment Generation:** Village and small-scale industries play a vital role in generating employment, particularly in rural areas where large industries are less prevalent.
 
• **Traditional Skills:** The committee emphasized utilizing traditional skills and crafts to preserve cultural heritage while boosting economic activities.

questions.question: Which stretch of the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system was declared as the National Waterway No.1 as per an Act in 1982?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad to Haldia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The stretch of the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from **Allahabad to Haldia** was declared as **National Waterway No. 1** in 1982 under the National Waterways Act.
 
• This waterway spans a length of approximately **1,620 kilometers**, making it the longest national waterway in India.
 
• National Waterway No. 1 plays a crucial role in facilitating **inland water transportation** for cargo and passenger movement between major cities and ports.
 
• The waterway passes through the states of **Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal**, connecting key economic hubs.
 
• The development and maintenance of this waterway are overseen by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Waterways in India:**

 
 
• India has identified a total of **111 National Waterways** for inland navigation under the National Waterways Act, 2016.
 
• National Waterway No. 1 (Allahabad to Haldia) was the first declared under the 1982 Act, setting the foundation for future waterways.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Inland Waterways:**
 
 
• Inland waterways are a **cost-effective and environmentally friendly** mode of transportation.
 
• They help reduce road congestion and lower carbon emissions by shifting bulk cargo transport to waterways.
 
 
 
• **Key Projects:**
 
 
• The **Jal Marg Vikas Project (JMVP)** was initiated to enhance navigation facilities along National Waterway No. 1.
 
• This project includes dredging, construction of terminals, and modernizing navigation systems.
 
 
 
• **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI):**
 
 
• Established in **1986**, IWAI is responsible for the development, maintenance, and regulation of inland waterways in India.
 
• IWAI promotes the use of waterways for transportation and ensures their integration with other modes of transport.

questions.question: Shahi Atala Masjid is located in which of the following district of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaunpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shahi Atala Masjid is a historical mosque located in **Jaunpur district**, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• It was constructed during the reign of **Ibrahim Shah Sharqi** in the 15th century (1408 AD).
 
• The mosque is an excellent example of **Sharqi architectural style**, blending Islamic and Indian design elements.
 
• The structure features massive gateways, intricate carvings, and a distinctive domed roof, making it a significant heritage site.
 
• It is one of the most iconic landmarks of Jaunpur and represents the city's rich historical and cultural legacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sharqi Dynasty:** The Sharqi dynasty ruled Jaunpur from the late 14th century to the early 16th century and was known for its patronage of art and architecture.
 
• **Architectural Features:** The mosque exhibits features like domes, arches, and intricate calligraphy, which are typical of medieval Islamic architecture.
 
• **Jaunpur:** Often referred to as the "Shiraz of India," Jaunpur is historically renowned for its architectural marvels built during the Sharqi Sultanate.
 
• **Preservation Efforts:** Shahi Atala Masjid is recognized as a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
 
• **Cultural Importance:** The mosque not only serves as a place of worship but also attracts tourists and historians interested in medieval Indian architecture.

questions.question: The tableau of which of the following states showcased its contributions in the Indian National Movement during the Republic Day Parade of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tableau of Punjab during the Republic Day Parade 2022 highlighted its significant contributions to the **Indian National Movement**.
 
• It paid tribute to freedom fighters like **Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev**, who played a pivotal role in India's struggle for independence.
 
• The tableau also showcased the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**, a tragic event that galvanized the freedom movement in India.
 
• Punjab's rich history in resisting colonial rule and its role in shaping the freedom struggle were key themes of the tableau.
 
• The state has a long-standing legacy of producing leaders and revolutionaries who made immense sacrifices for India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**

 
 
• Occurred on **13 April 1919** in Amritsar, Punjab.
 
• British troops under General Dyer fired on unarmed civilians, killing hundreds.
 
• This event became a turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, igniting widespread protests against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Shaheed Bhagat Singh:**
 
 
• Born on **28 September 1907** in Punjab.
 
• He was a revolutionary freedom fighter known for his role in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case** and his execution at the age of 23.
 
• Famous for his slogan "**Inquilab Zindabad**" (Long Live the Revolution).
 
 
 
• **Contribution of Punjab to the Indian National Movement:**
 
 
• Punjab played a central role in the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement.
 
• It was a hub of revolutionary activities, with organizations like the Ghadar Party originating from this region.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day Parade Tableau:**
 
 
• The tableau is a creative representation of a state's culture, history, or achievements showcased during the Republic Day Parade held on **26 January** every year.
 
• It is a platform for states and union territories to highlight their contributions to the nation.

questions.question: The first complete census of India was taken in the year of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1881**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first complete census of India was conducted in **1881** under the British administration.
 
• This census was organized under the supervision of **W.C. Plowden**, the then Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The 1881 census established a systematic and uniform approach to collecting demographic data across the entire British Indian territory.
 
• It provided comprehensive information on population size, sex ratio, literacy rates, and occupational distribution at that time.
 
• The census was conducted every 10 years thereafter and continues to be an essential tool for policy planning and administration in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:** A census is a systematic enumeration of a population, typically recording various details of individuals such as age, sex, occupation, and residence.
 
• **Historical Background:** Before 1881, partial or experimental censuses were conducted in some regions of India, with the first such attempt in **1801 in Madras Presidency**.
 
• **Modern Census:** Post-independence, India has conducted censuses starting from 1951, with the most recent being in **2011**. The 2021 census was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• **Global Context:** Census-taking is a global practice, with countries like the United States conducting their first census in **1790** and the UK in **1801**.
 
• **Significance:** Census data is crucial for governance, resource allocation, electoral representation, infrastructure development, and monitoring social and economic progress.

questions.question: Which of the following is inversely related to the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speculative demand for money**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Speculative demand for money** refers to the desire to hold money for investment purposes, especially when individuals expect bond prices to fall or interest rates to rise.
 
• This type of money demand is inversely related to the **rate of interest**, as higher interest rates make bonds and other financial assets more attractive.
 
• When interest rates are low, people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds due to the risk of capital losses if bond prices fall.
 
• Speculative demand is a key component of the liquidity preference theory developed by **John Maynard Keynes**.
 
• It plays a significant role in determining the overall demand for money in an economy, particularly during periods of economic uncertainty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical demand for money:** Based on the Quantity Theory of Money, it assumes money is held primarily for transaction purposes and is proportional to the level of income.
 
• **Transaction demand for money:** Refers to the need for money to carry out day-to-day transactions and is directly related to income levels.
 
• **Precautionary demand for money:** Represents money held for unexpected expenses or emergencies, often influenced by uncertainty and income stability.
 
• **Liquidity preference theory:** Proposed by Keynes, this theory categorizes money demand into three motives: transaction, precautionary, and speculative.
 
• **Interest rate dynamics:** Higher interest rates incentivize investments in bonds or financial assets, reducing speculative money demand, while lower rates encourage holding money due to reduced investment returns.

questions.question: The Sanatan Sangeet Sanskriti Award is given by the:

options.text: Ram Krishan and Sons Charitable Trust

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ram Krishan and Sons Charitable Trust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sanatan Sangeet Sanskriti Award is instituted by **Ram Krishan and Sons Charitable Trust**, which is a private entity focused on promoting Indian cultural heritage.
 
• The award aims to honor individuals who have made significant contributions to **Indian classical music and dance**.
 
• It serves as a platform for recognizing and encouraging traditional art forms that are an integral part of India's rich cultural legacy.
 
• Recipients of this award are often acclaimed artists known for their dedication and excellence in their respective fields of Indian classical arts.
 
• The trust actively works towards preserving and promoting India's musical traditions through various initiatives, including this award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Classical Music**:

 
 
• Indian classical music is categorized into two main traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• It is characterized by complex ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Prominent instruments include the sitar, tabla, veena, and mridangam.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance**:
 
 
• There are eight classical dance forms officially recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and Kathakali.
 
• Each dance form has unique techniques, music, costumes, and storytelling methods rooted in India's cultural and spiritual traditions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Cultural Trusts**:
 
 
• Cultural trusts like Ram Krishan and Sons Charitable Trust play a crucial role in preserving India's cultural heritage.
 
• They often organize events, provide scholarships, and recognize artists to promote traditional art forms.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**:
 
 
• It is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, established in 1952 by the Government of India.
 
• The Akademi provides support and recognition to artists and aims to preserve and propagate India's performing arts.

questions.question: _____, Chief Minister of Nagaland, hoisted the National Flag at the state level celebration of 76th Independence Day at Naga Civil Secretariat Plaza Kohima, on August 15, 2022.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Neiphiu Rio** is the Chief Minister of Nagaland and has been serving in this role since March 2018.
 
• On **August 15, 2022**, Neiphiu Rio hoisted the National Flag at the state-level celebration of the 76th Independence Day at Naga Civil Secretariat Plaza, Kohima.
 
• Rio is a veteran politician from Nagaland and a member of the Nationalist Democratic Progressive Party (**NDPP**).
 
• This Independence Day celebration marked the occasion of **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**, commemorating 75 years of India’s independence.
 
• Neiphiu Rio emphasized the importance of peace, development, and unity in his Independence Day speech during the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Nagaland:** Nagaland became the 16th state of India on December 1, 1963, and its capital is Kohima.
 
• **Neiphiu Rio's Leadership:** Under his leadership, Nagaland has focused on infrastructure development, peace talks, and resolving longstanding issues related to the insurgency.
 
• **National Flag Hoisting:** Hoisting the National Flag on Independence Day is a mark of respect and patriotism, symbolizing India's sovereignty and unity.

questions.question: Under Stand-Up India Scheme what is the maximum amount a bank can land as a loan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1 Crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Stand-Up India Scheme** was launched by the Government of India on **5th April 2016** to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and women entrepreneurs.
 
• Under this scheme, banks can provide loans ranging from **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** to at least one SC or ST borrower and one woman borrower per branch for setting up a greenfield enterprise.
 
• Loans are provided for **manufacturing, services, or trading sectors**, but the enterprise must be a new business (greenfield).
 
• The scheme is implemented through **Scheduled Commercial Banks**, and borrowers can apply directly at the bank branch, through the Stand-Up India portal, or via a Lead District Manager (LDM).
 
• The loan is repayable in a maximum of **7 years** with a moratorium period of up to 18 months.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Greenfield Enterprise:** This refers to a business that is being set up for the first time, as opposed to an expansion or diversification of an existing business.
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:** The applicant must belong to the SC/ST category or be a woman entrepreneur, and the business must involve a greenfield project in manufacturing, services, or trading.
 
• **Nature of Loan:** The loan under the Stand-Up India scheme is a composite loan, which includes a term loan and a working capital component.
 
• **Credit Guarantee:** The loans are backed by the **Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand-Up India (CGFSI)**, which provides a degree of risk coverage to the lenders.
 
• **Digital Platform:** The Stand-Up India portal (www.standupmitra.in) serves as a one-stop solution for information, application, and facilitation of loans under this scheme.

questions.question: Scientists from which institute have developed a portable, user-friendly, and non - invasive device for detecting oral cancer in resource-constrained clinical settings in January 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT, Kharagpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Scientists from **IIT Kharagpur** developed a portable, user-friendly, and non-invasive device for detecting oral cancer.
 
• The device was designed to be used in **resource-constrained clinical settings**, making it accessible to underserved populations.
 
• It leverages advanced technology to detect oral cancer at an **early stage**, improving the chances of effective treatment.
 
• The device is particularly useful in countries like India, where **oral cancer has a high prevalence** due to tobacco usage and other factors.
 
• This innovation aligns with the goal of providing affordable healthcare solutions and improving diagnostic accessibility in rural and urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oral Cancer:**

 
 
• Oral cancer refers to cancer of the mouth, lips, tongue, cheeks, and throat.
 
• Key risk factors include **tobacco consumption, alcohol use, and HPV infection**.
 
• Early detection is critical as it significantly improves survival rates.
 
 
 
• **Non-Invasive Diagnostic Devices:**
 
 
• Such devices do not require penetration into the body or tissue removal for diagnosis.
 
• They are preferred in **primary healthcare settings** due to their ease of use and patient comfort.
 
 
 
• **India's Oral Cancer Burden:**
 
 
• India accounts for approximately 30% of the world's oral cancer cases.
 
• The disease is often diagnosed at advanced stages, leading to high mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **IIT Kharagpur's Contributions:**
 
 
• IIT Kharagpur is known for its innovative healthcare solutions, including **low-cost diagnostic devices**.
 
• Its interdisciplinary research combines engineering, medicine, and technology to address critical public health challenges.

questions.question: Which one of the following was the last dynasty of Vijayanagar Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aravidu dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth and last dynasty of the Vijayanagar Empire, established by Tirumala Deva Raya.
 
• It was founded after the fall of the Tuluva dynasty and the catastrophic Battle of Talikota in 1565, which led to the decline of Vijayanagar's power.
 
• The Aravidu rulers tried to rebuild the empire but faced constant challenges from the Deccan Sultanates and internal strife.
 
• The dynasty lasted until the early 17th century, marking the end of the Vijayanagar Empire.
 
• Key rulers of the Aravidu dynasty include Tirumala Deva Raya and Sriranga Raya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagar Empire:**

 
 
• Founded in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya of the Sangama dynasty.
 
• Known for its architectural marvels, including Hampi, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It was one of the most prosperous empires in Indian history, renowned for trade, culture, and administration.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Talikota (1565):**
 
 
• Fought between the Vijayanagar Empire and a coalition of Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, and Bidar.
 
• The defeat marked the beginning of the decline of Vijayanagar and led to the sacking of Hampi.
 
 
 
• **Dynasties of Vijayanagar:**
 
 
• Sangama dynasty (1336–1485): Founders of the empire.
 
• Saluva dynasty (1485–1505): Brief reign with attempts to stabilize the empire.
 
• Tuluva dynasty (1505–1565): Golden age under Krishnadevaraya.
 
• Aravidu dynasty (1565–early 17th century): Last dynasty, marked by decline.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Vijayanagar:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire contributed significantly to South Indian culture, art, and temple architecture.
 
• Its administrative and military innovations were influential in shaping the region's history.
 
• Hampi remains a symbol of the empire's grandeur and achievements.

questions.question: The famous “Sundarbans Forests” are found in which of the following states of India ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sundarbans Forests are located in the state of **West Bengal**, India.
 
• This forest is part of the world's largest **mangrove ecosystem**, spanning across India and Bangladesh.
 
• The Indian Sundarbans are a UNESCO **World Heritage Site** and are recognized for their exceptional biodiversity.
 
• It is home to the **Bengal tiger**, one of the most iconic and endangered species in the world.
 
• The Sundarbans serve as a critical buffer zone, protecting the coastal regions from cyclones and tidal surges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology**:

 
 
• **Mangrove Forest:** A type of coastal wetland found in tropical and subtropical regions, characterized by salt-tolerant trees and shrubs.
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspot:** A region with significant levels of species richness that is under threat from human activities.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Significance**:
 
 
• The Sundarbans act as a carbon sink, helping mitigate climate change.
 
• The mangroves stabilize the coastline and prevent soil erosion.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**:
 
 
• In addition to the Bengal tiger, the Sundarbans host species like estuarine crocodiles, spotted deer, and various bird species.
 
• The region supports rare plant species like Sundari and Goran trees.
 
 
 
• **Threats**:
 
 
• Climate change and rising sea levels pose a major threat to the Sundarbans.
 
• Human activities like deforestation and habitat destruction further endanger the ecosystem.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the prominent figures of the Justice Party movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P Theagaraya Chetty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **P Theagaraya Chetty** was one of the founding members of the **South Indian Liberal Federation**, popularly known as the Justice Party, established in 1916.
 
• The Justice Party primarily represented the interests of the **non-Brahmin communities** in Tamil Nadu and worked towards achieving social justice and equality.
 
• Theagaraya Chetty was a key leader and advocate for **reservation in education and government jobs** for marginalized communities.
 
• He played a significant role in shaping the Justice Party's policies and ideology, which emphasized anti-Brahminism and social reform.
 
• The Justice Party, under leaders like Theagaraya Chetty, laid the foundation for the **Dravidian movement** that later gained prominence in Tamil Nadu politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Justice Party:**

 
 
• Founded in 1916 in Madras (now Chennai), it was a political organization advocating for the rights of non-Brahmins.
 
• The party's name was derived from its official newspaper, "Justice."
 
• It was instrumental in introducing **communal reservations** in government institutions in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Movement:**
 
 
• This socio-political movement originated from the ideologies of the Justice Party.
 
• It emphasized anti-casteism, rationalism, and self-respect, and opposed Brahminical dominance.
 
• Leaders like Periyar E.V. Ramasamy further developed the movement.
 
 
 
• **Reservation Policy:**
 
 
• The Justice Party was the first to implement communal reservation policies in education and employment in 1921.
 
• These policies aimed to uplift socially and economically disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy:**
 
 
• Though not a founding member, Periyar later became a prominent leader of the Justice Party.
 
• He transformed the party into a broader social reform movement, propagating the ideals of social justice and atheism.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India does not share the border with Nepal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nepal shares its border with five Indian states: **Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal,** and **Sikkim**.
 
• The state of **Himachal Pradesh does not share its border with Nepal**.
 
• Himachal Pradesh is located to the northwest of Uttarakhand and shares its borders with states like Punjab, Haryana, and Jammu & Kashmir, but not with Nepal.
 
• **Uttarakhand** and **Sikkim**, located along the northern part of India, directly share their borders with Nepal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India-Nepal Border:** The India-Nepal border stretches for approximately 1,850 kilometers and is an open border under the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship.
 
• **Uttarakhand:** Shares a border with Nepal through the districts of Pithoragarh, Champawat, and Udham Singh Nagar.
 
• **Sikkim:** Shares a small border with Nepal to its west, separated by the Mechi River.
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:** While located near the Himalayan region, it does not share any border with Nepal. Its neighbors include states like Punjab, Haryana, and regions like Ladakh.
 
• **Strategic Importance:** The India-Nepal border holds strategic importance due to trade, cultural ties, and geographical proximity, making it an area of bilateral cooperation and interaction.

questions.question: When was the master direction of RBI on microfinance loans implemented?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April 01, 2022**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued the **Master Direction on Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans**, which came into effect on **April 01, 2022**.
 
• The new regulatory framework aims to **standardize rules across all lenders** providing microfinance loans, including banks, NBFCs, and MFIs.
 
• It introduces a **common definition of microfinance loans**, removing the distinction between NBFC-MFIs and other lenders.
 
• Under this framework, **interest rate ceilings** on microfinance loans were removed, allowing lenders to determine rates transparently.
 
• The framework focuses on reducing **over-indebtedness** by capping the total loan repayment obligation of a household at 50% of its monthly income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance Loans:**

 
 
• These are small-ticket loans provided to low-income individuals or groups who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• Typically used for income-generating activities, microfinance loans aim to promote **financial inclusion**.
 
 
 
• **NBFC-MFIs:**
 
 
• Non-Banking Financial Companies-Microfinance Institutions primarily focus on providing microfinance loans to economically weaker sections.
 
• They were earlier subject to regulatory norms specific to the microfinance sector, such as interest rate caps.
 
 
 
• **Household Income Assessment:**
 
 
• As per the new framework, lenders must assess the household income of borrowers to ensure that loan repayments do not exceed 50% of income.
 
• This aims to prevent **over-indebtedness** and improve borrower financial health.
 
 
 
• **Transparency in Interest Rates:**
 
 
• The RBI now mandates lenders to disclose a comprehensive pricing structure, including interest rates, processing fees, and insurance charges.
 
• This is aimed at ensuring **transparency and fairness** for borrowers.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• The Master Direction is a step forward in promoting financial inclusion by creating a level playing field for all microfinance lenders.
 
• It focuses on empowering borrowers through **responsible lending practices**.

questions.question: In the year 1947, what was the literacy rate in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1947, the literacy rate in India was approximately **12% (0.12)**, reflecting the limited access to education during the colonial era.
 
• The literacy rate at the time was much lower for women, with female literacy being around **8%**.
 
• India's education system during British rule prioritized elite education and neglected mass education, contributing to the low literacy rate.
 
• Post-independence, the Indian government made significant efforts to improve literacy through policies like the **National Literacy Mission (1988)**.
 
• The literacy rate has steadily increased since independence, reaching **77.7% as per the 2017-18 National Sample Survey**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Definition:** Literacy is defined as the ability to read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• **National Literacy Mission:** Launched in 1988, this mission aimed to achieve 100% literacy for people aged 15-35 years.
 
• **Post-Independence Educational Reforms:** India established institutions like the University Grants Commission (UGC) and adopted policies such as the Right to Education Act (2009).
 
• **Gender Gap in Literacy:** While literacy rates have improved, disparities between male and female literacy persist, with males consistently having higher literacy rates.
 
• **Current Literacy Rate:** As of recent data, India's literacy rate has improved significantly, but challenges remain in rural areas and among marginalized communities.

questions.question: In which of the following months India-Maldives Joint Statement was released during the Official Visit of the President of the Maldives to India?

questions.question: The story of the monkey king is shown on a piece of sculpture found from a stupa at __________ in Central India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharhut**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The story of the monkey king is depicted on a piece of sculpture found at the ancient stupa of **Bharhut**, located in Central India.
 
• Bharhut is an archaeological site in Madhya Pradesh, renowned for its **Buddhist sculptures and inscriptions**.
 
• The stupa at Bharhut contains carvings that illustrate various Jataka tales, which are moral stories related to the previous lives of the Buddha.
 
• The monkey king story is part of the Jataka tales and symbolizes themes of leadership, sacrifice, and wisdom.
 
• The Bharhut sculptures are considered one of the earliest examples of **Buddhist art** in India, dating back to the Maurya and Sunga periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharhut Stupa:**

 
 
• The stupa was originally constructed during the reign of Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• It was later expanded and decorated with elaborate railings, pillars, and gateways during the Sunga period (2nd century BCE).
 
• The sculptures often include inscriptions that identify the donors and the stories depicted.
 
 
 
• **Jataka Tales:**
 
 
• The Jataka tales are a collection of stories recounting the previous lives of Gautama Buddha.
 
• They emphasize moral values such as compassion, selflessness, and wisdom.
 
• The monkey king story is one of the prominent Jataka tales that reflects leadership and sacrifice.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Art in India:**
 
 
• Early Buddhist art primarily focused on symbolic representations of Buddha and stories from his life.
 
• Sites like Bharhut, Sanchi, and Amaravati are famous for their contributions to Buddhist art.
 
• The carvings often depict flora, fauna, and scenes from daily life, reflecting a connection with nature.
 
 
 
• **Central Indian Archaeology:**
 
 
• Central India holds significant archaeological sites, including Bharhut, Sanchi, and Udayagiri caves.
 
• These sites provide valuable insights into early Indian art, architecture, and religion.
 
• They showcase the evolution of Buddhist and Hindu iconography over centuries.

questions.question: In the national movement of India, which of the following Committees/Commissions had demanded a bill of rights for Indians?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motilal Nehru Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Motilal Nehru Committee**, formed in 1928, was tasked with drafting a constitution for India as part of the Indian National Congress's efforts to demand self-rule.
 
• It was chaired by **Motilal Nehru** and included other prominent leaders such as Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The committee's report, known as the **Nehru Report**, included provisions for a **Bill of Rights**, ensuring fundamental rights for all Indians.
 
• The report advocated for **complete independence**, secularism, and equal rights irrespective of caste, creed, or gender.
 
• The recommendations of the Motilal Nehru Committee marked a significant step toward India's constitutional development and self-governance aspirations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bill of Rights**:

 
 
• A Bill of Rights is a formal declaration of the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed to individuals in a country.
 
• In the Nehru Report, it included rights such as freedom of speech, equality before the law, and protection against discrimination.
 
• It laid the foundation for similar provisions in India's later constitutions, including the Constitution of India adopted in 1950.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**:
 
 
• The Simon Commission, established by the British government in 1927, did not include Indian members, leading to widespread protests.
 
• Its exclusion of Indians highlighted the lack of self-determination and fueled demands for complete independence.
 
 
 
• **Cripps Mission**:
 
 
• The Cripps Mission, sent in 1942, proposed limited self-governance for India but failed to address the demand for complete independence.
 
• It did not include provisions for a Bill of Rights.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Nehru Report**:
 
 
• While the British government did not adopt the report, it unified Indians in their demand for rights and independence.
 
• It influenced later constitutional debates and the framing of India's Constitution post-independence.

questions.question: Which gadget developed by the Indian Institute of Technology, Ropar, resembles a USB flash drive, continuously records the temperature of its immediate surroundings “from -40 to +80 degrees in any time zone for a complete 90 days on a single charge
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AmbiTag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **AmbiTag** is a device developed by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar.
 
• This innovative gadget resembles a USB flash drive and is designed to record temperature data continuously.
 
• It can measure temperatures ranging from **-40°C to +80°C**, making it suitable for diverse climatic conditions.
 
• The device operates for a complete **90 days on a single charge**, offering long-term usability.
 
• AmbiTag is particularly useful for monitoring environmental conditions during the transportation of vaccines, food, and other temperature-sensitive products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperature Data Logger:** Devices like AmbiTag are categorized as temperature data loggers, which are widely used in industries like pharmaceuticals, food, and logistics to ensure quality control.
 
• **Vaccine Storage and Transport:** Maintaining precise temperature ranges is critical for vaccines, especially COVID-19 vaccines, which require cold chain management.
 
• **Importance of Temperature Monitoring:** Temperature fluctuations can degrade sensitive materials, leading to financial losses or compromised safety in healthcare and food industries.
 
• **USB Form Factor:** The USB-like design of AmbiTag enhances portability and ease of use, allowing users to download data directly to computers for analysis.
 
• **Innovation in India:** AmbiTag represents the growing focus on indigenous technological solutions by Indian academic institutions to address global challenges.
